. This is an appeal u/s 374 (3) of the Criminal Procedure Code for setting aside the impugned judgment dated 25.07.2023 and order on sentence dated 02.08.2023 passed by Ms. Moksha Bains,
Ld. M.M. NI. Act, South-East, Saket Court, New Delhi in case bearing CC No.12714/2019 titled as "Ajay Kumar Gupta vs Ajay Rao."

sentences.text: under Section 138 NI Act whereby accused was convicted for the offence u/s 138 NI Act and sentenced to pay fine as compensation of Rs.3,75,000/- within 60 days and in default of payment of fine, will undergo simple imprisonment for a period of three months.

2. Brief facts of the case of the complainant is that he had extended a friendly loan of Rs.3,00,000/-
to the accused for a period of 6-7 months.

In discharge of liability, the accused no.1 issued two cheques bearing no.831171 dated 15.04.2019 and No.831170 dated 24.04.2019 for an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- each (adding upto total of Rs.3,00,000/-) both drawn on State Bank of India, Deepak Building Branch-13, Nehru Place, New Delhi and upon presentation of the said cheques in Oriental Bank of Commerce, Mohan Co-op Industrial Estate, New Delhi-110044
, the same were returned unpaid with the remarks "Pl. Contract Drawer/Drawee vide return memo dated 25.04.2019.

After repeated reminders by the complainant for payment of consideration amount, accused failed to Ajay Rao vs Ajay Kumar Gupta on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154901230/
1 make payment to the complainant.

sentences.text: Thereafter, complainant sent a legal notice of demand dated 10.05.2019 to the accused u/s 138 of NI Act calling upon the accused within 15 days of the receipt of the legal notice as prescribed u/s 138 of the NI Act.
The legal notie of demand was duly served upon the accused.
Even after the expiry of 15 days stipulated period, the accused did not make the payment.
3. Thereafter, the complainant had filed a complaint case u/s. 138 N.I.Act and led pre-summoning evidence.
The appellant/accused was summoned and notice under Section 251 Cr.PC was framed against the accused and evidences were recorded and
after hearing the arguments, Ld. Trial Court passed the judgment dated 25.07.2023 and passed order on sentence dated 02.08.2023.
Feeling aggrieved, the accused has challenged the aforesaid impugned judgment and order on sentence by filing present appeal.

4. As the appeal was filed beyond limitation period, therefore, application for condonation of delay was moved on the ground that the counsel could not be contacted ensuring timely obtaining of certified copies of all relevant documents including copy of judgement /sentence for preparation of appeal although clear intimation / instruction was conveyed to the counsel.
The appellant has to go to Raipur with in short notice to attend his ailing mother at Raipur and the copy of the train ticket dated 24.08.2023 was annexed with.
After that the appellant suffered the paralytic attack on 28.09.2023 and he is still under medical observation and relevant medical reports are annexed with.
Further, appellant secured some reflief due to medical treatment, he got suffered a severe leg injury because of which he had to confine to bed for complete rest.
Therefore, it is prayed that delay in filing the appeal be condoned.
5. Counsel for the respondent did not file any reply to application for condonation of delay but orally argued that appellant has made wrong submissions and no ground is made to condone the delay.

He filed the copy of order dated 18.01.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court on application u/s 421 r/w 431 Cr.PC filed by the complianant/ respondent in which warrants of attachement were issued against the accused/ appellant and submitted that only after issuance of warrants of attachment he has filed the present appeal and it shows that delay in appeal is not bonafide but appeal is filed only after coercive action were initiated by the Ld. Trial Court.

He further submits that medical documents filed by the appellant are also genuine as in medical document dated 01.03.2024 it is mentioned that there is pain in left foot but X-ray of right foot was done.
It shows that medical documents are prepared, so that delay can be condoned.

6. Case file perused and detailed arguments heard.
7. The first ground taken by the appellant for explaining the delay was that his counsel could not be contacted because of which certified copies could not be obtained within time and appeal could not be prepared.
As per section 353 (4) Cr.PC when the judgment is pronounced the copy of same shall be provided free of cost to the convict.

So, copy of the judgment and order on sentence must have been provided by the Ld. Trial Court to the appellant/ accused on the day of pronouncement and same are Ajay Rao vs Ajay Kumar Gupta on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154901230/
2 sufficient to file the appeal.

sentences.text: There is no requirement of applying for certified copies of the judgment and order on sentence by the convict i.e. appellant in the present case.
So, this ground taken by the appellant appears to be after thought.
Further, this ground is also not supported by the documents annexed by the appellant with his application of condonation of delay.
He has stated that his counsel could not be contacted because of which certified copies could not be collected and appeal could not be prepared within time.
The train ticket of appellant to Raipur is of dated 24.08.2023 and he returned to Delhi on 23.09.2023, this shows that appellant/accused was not in Delhi during the above-mentioned period.
But certified copy of impugned order filed along with the appeal shows that it was collected on 02.09.2023 i.e. during the above-mentioned period when the accused/appellant was not in Delhi.
No clarification was given by the accused/appellant regarding the person who collected the certified copy.
As per rules only the party or his counsel can collect the certified copies, therefore, the certified copies must have been collected by the counsel for appellant/accused.
So, false ground has been taken by the appellant that his counsel was not in contact because of which appeal could not be filed within time.
8. Submission made by the counsel of the respondent are correct that in medical document dated 03.01.2024, C/o (L) foot pain but the X-ray report of right foot is filed.
Further, the medical condition of the accused/appellant was not such that he could not contact his lawyer and get the appeal prepared.

9. It is clear that only after the passing of order dated 18.01.2024 by the Ld. Trial Court, wherein warrants of attachment and NBWs were issued against the appellant/accused he has filed the present appeal.

Even if, court takes a lenient view and does not consider the period from 24.08.2023 i.e. day he left the Delhi for Raipur, till 16.01.2024 i.e. day proxy counsel for the accused appeared before Ld. Trial Court, even then, appeal is filed after 45 days of passing of impugned order on sentence dated 02.08.2023.
As per section 389 Cr.PC the appeal is to be filed within 30 days but appeal is filed after 45 days and there is delay of 15 days.
It is settled law that each day delay has to be explained but no explanation is on the record regarding delay of above-mentioned dates.

10. In "Rishi Prabhat v. Delhi Development Authority", (1994) 1 CCC 719 (Del), it has been held that to obtain extension of time by invoking the provisions of section 5 of the Act, the party seeking extension has to satisfy the court that he had sufficient cause for not filing suit, appeal, revision or objections, within the prescribed time.

entities.text: Rishi Prabhat v. Delhi Development Authority", (1994) 1 CCC 719 (Del)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But in the present case, no reason except that appellant was undergoing medical treatment is mentioned and as discussed above, medical problem was not such which prevented him to seek his judicial remedy and his ground are also found to be false.
Therefore, in the opinion of court, no sufficient cause has been shown by the applicant for not filing the appeal within statutory period.

11. In "Ramlal v. Rewa Coalfields Ltd.", AIR 1962 SC 361, if the party who has applied for extension of period shows that the delay was due to any of the facts mentioned in the explanation that would be treated as sufficient cause, and after it is treated as sufficient cause, the question may then arise whether discretion should be exercised in favour of the party or not.

entities.text: Ramlal v. Rewa Coalfields Ltd.", AIR 1962 SC 361
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As in the present case, no sufficient cause has been shown by the appellant, therefore, there is no question of exercising discretion in his favour by the court.

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C) Nos.
2054-2055/2022

in case titled "LINGESWARAN Etc. Vs. Thirunagalingam decided on 25.02.2022 has held that :
"5.
We are in complete agreement with the view taken by the High Court.

Once it was found even by the learned trial Court that delay has not been properly explained and even there are no merits in the application for condonation of delay, thereafter, the matter should rest there and the condonation of delay application was required to be dismissed.

The approach adopted by the learned trial Court that, even after finding that, in absence of any material evidence it cannot be said that the delay has been explained and that there are no merits in the application, still to condone the delay would be giving a premium to a person who fails to explain the delay and who is guilty of delay and laches.
At this stage, the decision of this Court in the case of Popat Bahiru Goverdhane v. Land Acquisition Officer, reported in (2013) 10 SCC 765 is required to be referred to.

entities.text: Popat Bahiru Goverdhane v. Land Acquisition Officer, reported in (2013) 10 SCC 765
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, it is observed and held that the law of limitation may harshly affect a particular party but it has to be applied with all its rigour when the statute so prescribes.
The Court has no power to extend the period of limitation on equitable grounds.
The statutory provision may cause hardship or inconvenience to a particular party but the Court has no choice but to enforce it giving full effect to the same.

5.1 In the case of Maniben Devraj Shah v. Municipal Corporation of Brihan Mumbai,
(2012) 5 SCC 157, in paragraph 14, it is observed and held as under:
"The law of limitation is founded on public policy. The limitation Act, 1963 has not been enacted with the object of destroying the rights of the parties but to ensure that they approach the court for vindication of their rights without unreasonable delay.

entities.text:
Maniben Devraj Shah v. Municipal Corporation of Brihan Mumbai,
(2012) 5 SCC 157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The idea underlying the concept of limitation is that every remedy should remain alive only till the expiry of the period fixed by the legislature.
At the same time, the courts are empowered to condone the delay provided that sufficient cause is shown by the applicant for not availing the remedy within the prescribed period of limitation."
6. In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, we are in complete agreement with the view taken by the High Court.
The Special 4 Leave Petitions stand dismissed".

13. Considering the mandate given in the above-mentioned judgment and the discussion done hereinabove, court refuses to condone the delay in filing the appeal within the statutory period of limitation.
Therefore, application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal is hereby dismissed and consequentially appeal is dismissed.
14. Ld. Trial Court is directed to take the necessary steps to execute the order on sentence passed by it on 02.08.2023.
